Harness plugin that starts each Vercel AI Gateway conversation on the fastest provider for its model
# dsh-fastcel
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that starts each Vercel AI Gateway conversation on the fastest provider fo
r its model. It is the harness edition of fastcel, the Oh My Pi plugin.
Vercel AI Gateway serves many models through several providers, and their speeds differ a lot. `deep
seek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` has 22 providers. On one afternoon the fastest, subconscious, produce
d a median of 394 tokens per second over the last hour, and the slowest measured, runinfra, 42. Left
to choose, the gateway sent three test requests to baseten (175 tok/s). With fastcel the same reque
st went to subconscious.
## How it works
fastcel decides the order in which providers are tried. Vercel decides how long a conversation stays
on the provider it landed on.
### fastcel ranks the providers
On every model call the harness sends to `ai-gateway.vercel.sh`, fastcel attaches the model's provid
the harness sends to `ai-gateway.vercel.sh`, fastcel attaches the model's providers, fastest first:
1. It reads the provider stats from `GET /v1/models/{model}/endpoints`. This is public data, the sam
e figures shown on the model's page at vercel.com/ai-gateway/models, and needs no key. The stats are
cached per model for 15 minutes. Once they are stale, requests keep using them while a refresh runs

in the background.
2. It orders the providers by median throughput over the last hour. A provider g
oes to the back of the list when it is deprecated, when fewer than 90% of its requests succeeded in
the last 15 minutes, when the request has tools and the provider does not support them, or when its

context window is smaller than the conversation.
3. It sends the list as `providerOptions.gateway.or
der`. If the first provider fails, the gateway falls back through the rest in speed order.
fastcel keeps no ranking between requests: each one carries the ranking as it stands at that moment.
If the stats cannot be loaded, the request goes out unchanged and the gateway chooses as usual.
### Vercel keeps a conversation on one provider
The gateway does not simply take the first provider on the list. Its session affinity, on by default
, remembers which provider answered a conversation's previous message and tries that provider first,
so its prompt cache stays warm. In a session this plays out as follows:
1. **First message.** No provider is remembered yet, so the message goes to the top of fastcel's lis

t.
2. **Following messages.** They stay on that provider, even if fastcel's ranking changes in the m

eantime.
3. **After a pause or a failure.** Vercel forgets the provider once the conversation has be
en idle longer than that provider's cache lifetime: about 5 minutes for most providers, 10 for OpenA
I and Azure, and 1 hour for DeepSeek's own API. It also forgets it when the provider fails a request
. The next message goes to whichever provider is fastest at that point, and the conversation stays t
next message goes to whichever provider is fastest at that point, and the conversation stays there.
A new session or a subagent counts as a new conversation, so it starts on whichever provider is fast
subagent counts as a new conversation, so it starts on whichever provider is fastest when it begins.
### How it hooks into the harness
The harness's pi-ai adapter builds the gateway request itself and offers no hook to change its body,
so fastcel works at two layers:
- An `llm/stream` listener wraps every model call in a request scope that knows the session and how

many tokens its conversation held after the previous call.
- A hook on the process's `fetch` changes
a request only when it comes from such a scope, is a `POST` to an inference endpoint of `https://ai
-gateway.vercel.sh` (`/v1/messages`, `/v1/chat/completions` or `/v1/responses`), and its JSON body n
ames a model. It adds the order, sends the request, and reads the gateway's routing record from the
reply as it streams by, unchanged.
Every other request in the process is forwarded untouched. Stopping the plugin removes the hook.
### Details
- **Routing already in the request wins.** A request whose body already carries `providerOptions.gat

eway.order` or `.only` is sent as it is.
- **Some providers are skipped for your account.** Vercel m
arks some providers `plan_not_eligible` for some models. The gateway then moves on to the next provi

der in the list without trying the skipped one.
- **Why not `sort: "tps"`.** The gateway can sort pr
oviders by throughput itself, but when fastcel was tested most providers had no value in that sort,
so faster providers came after slower ones; see fastcel's notes. fastcel ranks with the endpoint sta
roviders came after slower ones; see fastcel's notes. fastcel ranks with the endpoint stats instead.
## Install
**Requires:** DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.2** (tested, web profile), Node.js **22+**, and a `vercel-
ai-gateway` route on the harness's pi-ai adapter, for example in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

Any pi-ai route whose endpoint is `https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh` works; fastcel recognizes the gatew
ay by the host each request goes to, not by the route's name.
From this repository, run:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then restart the harness. Install, restart or remove the plugin only when no reply is being generate
d. To remove it, run `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-fastcel` and restart.
## Use
Pick any Vercel AI Gateway model. fastcel shows the top of its current ranking, the provider and its
speed, with a ⚡ in front:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
It sits below the composer of a session, and in the options row above the composer on the New Sessio
n page. It is hidden when the selected model does not go through the gateway.
When the model's maker serves it from its own API, that provider has the maker's name, so the panel
marks it first-party, and the pick reads `deepseek (first-party) · 191 tok/s`. That means DeepSeek's
own API, not the DeepSeek model.
A conversation that started earlier can still be on another provider, as described above. The panel
shows where the last reply actually went.
